meta.title: MODERN SOCIETY AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
meta.titleVi: Xã hội hiện đại và phát triển bền vững

reading1.passage:
Modern cities are growing quickly. More people move to cities because they want better jobs, education and services. However, fast growth can create problems for the environment.

One important problem is pollution. Cars, factories and other activities can make the air less clean. Heavy traffic can also make city life uncomfortable. For this reason, many cities are trying to improve public transport. Buses, trains and other forms of public transportation can help people travel without using a private car every day.

Cities can also reduce waste. People can recycle paper, plastic, glass and metal instead of throwing everything away. Recycling can reduce the amount of rubbish that goes to landfills. Some cities also encourage people to reuse bags, bottles and other products.

Education is another important part of a better city. Good education can help young people develop useful skills. These skills may help them find jobs and take part in the local economy. A strong economy can provide more opportunities for families.

Cities also need green spaces. Parks can provide a healthy environment for people and can protect small animal habitats. In some areas, local governments work with communities on conservation projects. These projects may protect trees, rivers and animals.

A successful city does not only need new buildings. It also needs clean air, useful transport, good education and careful use of natural resources. Small changes by individuals, businesses and governments can make cities healthier and more comfortable places to live.

reading2.passage:
Many countries are changing rapidly as cities become larger and economies become more connected. This development can bring better jobs, improved education and new services. However, it can also put pressure on the environment and natural resources. For this reason, governments and communities are looking for ways to create more sustainable places to live.

One major concern is pollution. Growing numbers of cars can produce harmful emissions, while factories may also affect air and water quality. Better transport systems can help reduce some of these problems. Public buses, trains and cycling facilities can give people alternatives to private vehicles. If public transportation is convenient and affordable, more people may choose to use it.

Waste management is another important issue. Many products are used for a short time and then thrown away. Recycling allows some materials to be processed and used again. Recyclable paper, glass and plastic can therefore remain useful instead of becoming waste. However, recycling alone is not enough. People also need to reduce unnecessary consumption and reuse products whenever possible.

Economic development is closely connected to these environmental issues. A strong economy can create jobs and provide money for public services. At the same time, businesses need workers with suitable skills. Good education can help students acquire these skills and prepare them for changing job markets. In this way, education can support both individuals and the wider economy.

Sustainable development also requires the protection of natural areas. Forests, rivers and wetlands provide important habitats for many species. The loss of these habitats can reduce biodiversity. Conservation programmes can help preserve important natural areas, but they often require cooperation between governments, businesses and local communities.

A sustainable city therefore needs more than economic growth. It needs a balance between development, environmental protection and quality of life. Transport systems should be efficient, waste should be managed responsibly, and education should prepare people for future employment. When these areas work together, communities can become healthier and more resilient.

listening.passage:
Good morning, everyone. Today we are going to talk about how our town can become a better place to live.

First, we need to think about the environment. At the moment, air pollution is a problem, especially on busy roads. One possible solution is to improve public transport. If buses are comfortable and reliable, more people may use them instead of private cars.

We also need to deal with waste. Our town produces a lot of rubbish every day. People can recycle paper, plastic and glass. Recycling can reduce waste and save useful materials.

Education is another important area. Schools can teach students about environmental problems and help them develop useful skills. These skills may also help young people find jobs in the future.

A healthy economy is important for the town. Local businesses need workers with different abilities, and a good market can create opportunities for both businesses and customers.

Finally, we should protect natural areas outside the town. Some forests and rivers provide an important habitat for animals. Local groups are planning a conservation project to protect these areas.

If people, businesses and the local government work together, our town can become cleaner, healthier and more successful.
